title: Ellis Canning Co. v. International Harvester Co. (1953)
summary: The fully subrogated insurer, rather than the compensated insured, held the claim under the law applied.
notes:
This state decision is not a substitute for the full text and cure provisions of Federal Rule 17. Partial payment can raise a different party problem because more than one person may retain an interest.

The Kansas Supreme Court held that an insured fully paid by its insurer (Potomac Insurance Co.) is not the real party in interest under the Kansas code and cannot sue in its own name 'for the use and benefit of' the insurer; the result would differ for partial subrogation, where insured and insurer each hold part of the claim.

sections.Parties: Ellis Canning brought an action arising from damage to its equipment after its insurer had compensated the loss.
sections.Material Facts: The claim concerned negligent servicing of a tractor and resulting fire damage. The insurer paid the loss in full and became subrogated to the corresponding claim. The insured nevertheless sought to pursue the action in its own name.
sections.Procedural History: The Kansas court considered the objection that the action had not been brought by the real party in interest and sustained that objection.
sections.Issue: Who was entitled to bring the claim after the insurer fully paid the insured loss?
sections.Holding: The insurer held the fully subrogated claim and was the real party in interest under the law applied.
sections.Reasoning: The rule focused on who possessed the substantive right, rather than simply who originally suffered the damage. Full payment and subrogation transferred the claim in the manner relevant to the case. The decision introduces real-party analysis, which is distinct from standing, capacity, and the procedural permission to join additional claims.

learning.why: The fully subrogated insurer, rather than the compensated insured, held the claim under the law applied.

topics.cp-real-party: Payment and subrogation determined who held the claim being enforced.
topics.cp-joinder: Identifying the proper claimant precedes deciding which claims may be combined.
topics.cp-frcp-17: The Kansas real-party-in-interest statute parallels Rule 17(a), and the subrogation problem is the standard Rule 17 example.
